industry: Pest control (general pest, termite, rodent, mosquito)
words_and_claims_to_avoid: Government look-alike design, 'official notice', fake checks or invoices (39 USC 3001)
Unsubstantiated 'best', '#1', 'voted #1', 'guaranteed results', percent-savings claims (FTC Act s.5)
Invented or composite testimonials, star ratings or review counts (16 CFR 255)
'Free' unless it truly costs nothing and carries no hidden obligation (16 CFR 251)
Fake expiration dates or fake scarcity; any deadline printed must be real
Demographic/age targeting language (e.g., 'seniors', 'retirees') unless the client has evidence it fits their actual buyers
Any vendor case-study result (calls, ROI, revenue) printed as if it were the client's own result
'Safe', 'harmless', 'non-toxic', 'nonpoisonous', 'pet-safe', 'kid-safe', 'family-safe', 'safe for the environment' (federal + state pesticide rules)
'Pest-free guaranteed', 'kills 100%', 'eliminates all' without substantiation and a real guarantee

'Prevents disease', 'protects your family's health', 'stops Lyme/West Nile' or similar disease claims unless the product label supports them (EPA bars disease/health-protection implications on many labels)
'Pest-free' as a promise (GOLD-002 'pest-free this summer'); use 'fewer pests' or a re-service guarantee
Children or pets shown in or near a just-treated area (implied safety; NJ bans misleading pictures)
Fake 'violation' or 'inspection notice' designs that look like a city/county notice (39 USC 3001; CO also bans impersonating inspectors)
compliance_notes: If the sale closes in the home: FTC Cooling-Off Rule (16 CFR 429) applies to $25+ in-home sales; the client's contract must carry the 3-day cancel notice. States can add longer windows.
Any discount or 'save X%' must be off a real, recently charged price; 'save 40%' with no reference price is not allowed.

FTC 'Free' Guide, 16 CFR 251 (verified): (1) 'free with purchase' means the paid item is at its regular price (sold openly for about 30 days), with no markup or downgrade to cover the free item; (2) all conditions go right next to the offer, not in an asterisk footnote; (3) if the main job is priced by negotiation or bid, 'free [item] with purchase' is improper; (4) don't run the same 'free' offer more than 6 months in any 12; (5) 'gift' or 'bonus' wording doesn't cure a deceptive 'free'.

Warranty ads, 16 CFR 239 + 702 (verified): 'lifetime/life' must say whose or what life (239.4); 'satisfaction/money-back guarantee' only if the full price is refunded on request, with conditions disclosed (239.3); advertise a warranty only if it is promptly honored (239.5); ads should say where the full warranty can be seen (239.2).
Testimonials and star ratings must be real, typical and current; disclose any material connection (16 CFR 255).

Pesticide safety claims (verified): never say 'safe', 'harmless', 'non-toxic', 'nonpoisonous', 'pet-safe', 'kid-safe', 'eco-safe', with or without 'when used as directed'. Federal label rule 40 CFR 156.10(a)(5)(ix)-(x); explicit ad bans in TX (4 TAC 7.152), NJ (N.J.A.C. 7:30-2.12), CA (16 CCR 1999.5) and CO (C.R.S. 35-9-120). Assume every state is at least this strict until the client confirms.
No 'EPA approved', 'EPA registered' or anything implying government endorsement (40 CFR 156.10(a)(5)(v); TX 7.152(a)(5); CA 1999.5).
'Organic', 'natural', 'green', 'environmentally friendly' for pesticide services are banned outright in TX and NJ and need narrow substantiation elsewhere (FTC Green Guides 16 CFR 260).

Effectiveness claims ('kills 100%', 'pest-free guaranteed', 'eliminates') need substantiation and must match the product label (FIFRA s.12; TX 7.152(a)(11); CA 1999.5(f)(14)). Prefer outcome language with a re-service guarantee.
Show the licensed business name (TX requires it in every ad); NJ license references must include the word 'pesticide'. Don't advertise services the client isn't licensed for.
Pictures count: NJ bans misleading pictorial ads, so no children or pets playing in a just-treated area implying safety.
Florida, Texas and others treat termite work as regulated (inspection reports, contracts); state-specific termite advertising rules beyond the four states above were not verified.
Insurance fact on a card: cite the source ('Insurance Information Institute') and say 'usually' or 'typically': policies vary.
If the pest service sells in-home (e.g., termite contract after inspection) for $25+, Cooling-Off applies; buyer-requested emergency visits need a signed handwritten waiver to be excluded.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear, disgust, joy, pride, status, relief are all options; the client chooses.
Every angle and combo carries a sell-the-outcome line.
Unverified (agency/vendor-only) results are labeled; never quote them as fact on a card.

emotion_by_offer.why: A seen pest is a disgust trigger (Curtis et al. 2011); the card must deliver an immediate, confident fix. GOLD-005 'They're coming' and GOLD-010 'Seen one this summer?' open the loop.
emotion_by_offer.reinforcing_photo: Single isolated pest macro (small) + clean, calm home (large).
emotion_by_offer.what_backfires: Swarm/gore imagery with no fix; graphic pests the reader wants to throw away; '24/7' or 'same-day' that isn't true.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: GOLD-pest-control-002 'Keep your home pest-free this summer' vs effectiveness-substantiation rules (TX 7.152(a)(11), CA 1999.5)
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins: use 'fewer pests' or pair 'pest-free' with a real re-service guarantee; never promise it outright.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Common pest marketing 'safe for kids and pets' / 'eco-friendly' vs 40 CFR 156.10 and TX/NJ/CA/CO ad bans
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: banned outright. Sell the outcome (a calm home) instead of safety.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Disgust/swarm imagery (GOLD-005 'They're coming') vs C-3PO P6 'consequence carefully'
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Both allowed. Keep the pest small and crisp, pair with a calm fix image; avoid cheap gore. Client chooses intensity.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Vendor ROI figures (GOLD-007 964%, GOLD-008 1,204%) vs never print unverified numbers
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Unaudited vendor claims; use only as weak evidence that plan and lapsed-customer offers can work.
